## JUCE: a multi-purpose audio framework (Tutorial) {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 95%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- Open the Projucer and select `New Project` from the `File` menu.
- On the left-most menu, select `Application/Audio`, and in exporters, select `Xcode (macOS)` if you're on macOS, or `Visual Studio 2026` if you're on Windows. Name the project `Ringmod` and click `Create Project`.
- Let's now verify that the template builds correctly.
:::
- Now before we use our **Ringmod code** in the framework, we need to make little changes to it first: for instance, make the `SAMPLE_RATE` and the `BUFFER_SIZE` **constants** variable.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="1-21|4,6,9,12,13,15|23,27-28|37-39|50-51|50-51,57-59,62-66|68-70" filename="sinewave.cpp"}
struct Phasor {
    float phase;
    float frequency;
    float sample_rate;

    void init(float freq, float sr) {
        phase = 0;
        frequency = freq;
        sample_rate = sr;
    }

    void process(float buffer[], int nsamples) {
        for (int i = 0; i < nsamples; ++i) {
            buffer[i] = phase;
            phase += frequency/sample_rate;
            if (phase >= 1.f) {
                phase -= 1.f;
            }
        }
    }
};

struct Sinewave {
    Phasor phasor;
    float table[TABLE_SIZE];

    void init(float freq, float sr) {
        phasor.init(freq, sr);
        for (int x = 0; x < TABLE_SIZE; x++) {
            float fx = float(x);
            float phase = fx / TABLE_SIZE;
            float y = sin(phase * M_PI * 2.f);
            table[x] = y;
        }
    }

    void process(float buffer[], int nsamples) {
        phasor.process(buffer, nsamples);
        for (int i = 0; i < nsamples; ++i) {
            int x = int(buffer[i] * TABLE_SIZE);
            buffer[i] = table[x];
        }
    }
};

struct Ringmod {
    Sinewave carrier;  
    Sinewave modulator;
    float amplitude = 0.25;
    float* carrier_buffer;
    float* mod_buffer;

    void init(float c, float m, float sr, int nsamples) {
        // Initialize carrier & modulator:
        carrier.init(c, sr);
        modulator.init(m, sr);
        // Allocate intermediate buffers:
        carrier_buffer = new float[nsamples];
        mod_buffer = new float[nsamples];
    }

    ~Ringmod() {
        // Deallocate buffers in destructor:
        delete [] carrier_buffer;
        delete [] mod_buffer;
    }

    void process(float buffer[], int nsamples) {
        carrier.process(carrier_buffer, nsamples);
        modulator.process(mod_buffer, nsamples);

        for (int i = 0; i < nsamples; i++) {
             buffer[i] = carrier_buffer[i] * mod_buffer[i]
                       * amplitude;
        }
    }
};

```
:::
::::

- **JUCE projects** are usually structured in the following way:
:::
- For our first `Ringmod` standalone, we have 3 files in the `Source/` directory. `MainComponent.h & .cpp` are the files that are going to be implemented with our simple ringmod algorithm.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.text code-line-numbers="" filename="JUCE/Project"}
- Main.cpp # The application entrypoint (nothing to do here)
- MainComponent.h # Our new Audio module (header)
- MainComponent.cpp # Our new Audio module (source)
```
:::

#pragma once

#include <JuceHeader.h>

// --------------------------------------------------------
// Our pasted code:
// --------------------------------------------------------
struct Phasor { ... };
struct Sinewave { ... };
struct Ringmod { ... };

// --------------------------------------------------------
// JUCE code
// --------------------------------------------------------

- **JUCE projects** are usually structured in the following way:
- For our first `Ringmod` standalone, we have 3 files in the `Source/` directory. `MainComponent.h & .cpp` are the files that are going to be implemented with our simple ringmod algorithm.
- First, let's paste our `Ringmod` code in `MainComponent.h`.
:::
- In the **JUCE API**, the equivalent of our `init(...)` method would be `prepareToPlay(...)` and the one for our `process(...)` method would be `getNextAudioBlock(...)`.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="17|19" filename="Ringmod/Source/MainComponent.h"}
#pragma once

#include <JuceHeader.h>

// --------------------------------------------------------
// Our pasted code:
// --------------------------------------------------------
struct Phasor { ... };
struct Sinewave { ... };
struct Ringmod { ... };

// --------------------------------------------------------
// JUCE code
// --------------------------------------------------------
class MainComponent  : public juce::AudioAppComponent {

    void prepareToPlay(int samplesPerBlockExpected, double sampleRate) override;

    void getNextAudioBlock(const juce::AudioSourceChannelInfo& bufferToFill) override;
    
};
```

- **JUCE projects** are usually structured in the following way:
- For our first `Ringmod` standalone, we have 3 files in the `Source/` directory. `MainComponent.h & .cpp` are the files that are going to be implemented with our simple ringmod algorithm.
- First, let's paste our `Ringmod` code in `MainComponent.h`.
- In the **JUCE API**, the equivalent of our `init(...)` method would be `prepareToPlay(...)` and the one for our `process(...)` method would be `getNextAudioBlock(...)`.
:::
- We now need to write the *glue* between **our code** and the **JUCE API**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="21-24" filename="Ringmod/Source/MainComponent.h"}
#pragma once

#include <JuceHeader.h>

// --------------------------------------------------------
// Our pasted code:
// --------------------------------------------------------
struct Phasor { ... };
struct Sinewave { ... };
struct Ringmod { ... };

// --------------------------------------------------------
// JUCE code
// --------------------------------------------------------
class MainComponent  : public juce::AudioAppComponent {

    void prepareToPlay(int samplesPerBlockExpected, double sampleRate) override;

    void getNextAudioBlock(const juce::AudioSourceChannelInfo& bufferToFill) override;

private:
    //==============================================================================
    // Your private member variables go here...
    Ringmod rm;
    
};
```

## JUCE: a multi-purpose audio framework (Tutorial) {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 90%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- **JUCE projects** are usually structured in the following way:
- For our first `Ringmod` standalone, we have 3 files in the `Source/` directory. `MainComponent.h & .cpp` are the files that are going to be implemented with our simple ringmod algorithm.
- First, let's paste our `Ringmod` code in `MainComponent.h`.
- In the **JUCE API**, the equivalent of our `init(...)` method would be `prepareToPlay(...)` and the one for our `process(...)` method would be `getNextAudioBlock(...)`.
:::
- We now need to write the *glue* between **our code** and the **JUCE API**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="" filename="Ringmod/Source/MainComponent.cpp"}
void MainComponent::prepareToPlay (int samplesPerBlockExpected, double sampleRate)
{
    // This function will be called when the audio device is started, or when
    // its settings (i.e. sample rate, block size, etc) are changed.

    // You can use this function to initialise any resources you might need,
    // but be careful - it will be called on the audio thread, not the GUI thread.

    // For more details, see the help for AudioProcessor::prepareToPlay()
    rm.init(440.f, 20.f, sampleRate, samplesPerBlockExpected);
}
```

## JUCE: a multi-purpose audio framework (Tutorial) {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns .faust-layout}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {style="font-size: 90%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- **JUCE projects** are usually structured in the following way:
- For our first `Ringmod` standalone, we have 3 files in the `Source/` directory. `MainComponent.h & .cpp` are the files that are going to be implemented with our simple ringmod algorithm.
- First, let's paste our `Ringmod` code in `MainComponent.h`.
- In the **JUCE API**, the equivalent of our `init(...)` method would be `prepareToPlay(...)` and the one for our `process(...)` method would be `getNextAudioBlock(...)`.
:::
- We now need to write the *glue* between **our code** and the **JUCE API**.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
```{.cpp code-line-numbers="" filename="Ringmod/Source/MainComponent.cpp"}
void MainComponent::getNextAudioBlock (const juce::AudioSourceChannelInfo& bufferToFill)
{
    // Your audio-processing code goes here!

    // For more details, see the help for AudioProcessor::getNextAudioBlock()

    // Right now we are not producing any data, in which case we need to clear the buffer
    // (to prevent the output of random noise)
    bufferToFill.clearActiveBufferRegion();
    // Get write access to left channel & right channel pointers:
    float* ptr = bufferToFill.buffer->getWritePointer(0);
    float* ptr2 = bufferToFill.buffer->getWritePointer(1);

    // Process ringmod (only one channel)
    rm.process(ptr, bufferToFill.numSamples);

    // Copy the buffer to the right channel to make it stereo:
    memcpy(ptr2, ptr, bufferToFill.numSamples * sizeof(float));
}

```
